title: Engineer Equipment Maintenance Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-919A. Military Occupational Specialty 919A--Engineer Equipment Maintenance Warrant Officer
(Effective 202510)
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
    b. Prerequisites. AR 135-100, DA Pam 601-6, and DA Pam 611-21.
    c. MOS 919A. MOS 919A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are: 91B, 91C, 91D, 91H,
91J, 91L, 91X, and 91Z.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASIs associated with all warrant
officer MOS)).
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must--
               (a) Complete the Engineer Equipment Maintenance Warrant Officer Basic Course.
               (b) Have correctable vision, normal color discrimination, normal hearing, and full use of upper
and lower extremities per AR 40-501.
               (c) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security eligibility of SECRET.
         (2) CW3 must—See MOS 915T.

        (3) CW4 must—See MOS 915T.
        (4) CW5 must—See MOS 915E.
    g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2--
              (a) Supervises personnel in maintenance of engineer and ground support equipment.
              (b) Analyzes malfunctions and supervises minor repair and adjustment of engineer
equipment utilized for power generation, earthmoving, shaping and compacting, lifting and loading,
quarrying and rock crushing, asphalt concrete mixing and surfacing, water purification, refrigeration and
air conditioning, water gap crossing, POL transfer and engineer electronic application.
              (c) Supervises maintenance of non-engineer equipment assigned by equipment authorization
documents.
              (d) Inspects incoming equipment to determine repair requirements, assigns work to
subordinates, and ensures quality of work performed by inspection of outgoing equipment.
              (e) Establishes maintenance and repair schedules based on equipment schedules and
availability of parts, tools, and personnel and unit mission.
              (f) Establishes internal administrative procedures to procure, store, and issue publications,
tools, parts, and POL.
              (g) Manages maintenance float items to replace equipment not repairable within prescribed
time limits.
        (2) CW3—See MOS 915T

        (3) CW4—See MOS 915T.
        (4) CW5—See MOS 915E.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
           (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
           (2) A minimum OPAT score of (Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw (PT) -
0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles) is required in
Physical Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
           (3) Authorized position titles are provided in appendixes B and C. The following grades are used
to code positions into one of four definable skill levels: W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4
equals CW4; W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-919A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-919A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
